elements.scope_reason: Red-box header: presenting complaint 'anal symptoms' AND any-of the criteria below
elements.problem: Structure (and <complaint> (or ...)) matches the house standard. Minor: 'Anal finding' is not a recorded common symptom or warning sign, and its descendants include neutral findings such as 'Anus normal'; it works as an anchor only if anal complaints are recorded under it.
evidence: Urgent: anal symptoms with extremely painful lump or unable to pass stool :: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Anal finding" "finding")) (or (and ...Perianal lump... ...Anal pain Severe...) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Does not defecate" "finding"))))
Check for urgent anal symptom conditions :: due_to (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Anal finding" "finding"))

elements.problem: 'Extremely painful lump on anus' is encoded as Perianal lump AND Anal pain qualified Severe. 'Severe' stands in for 'extremely', which is acceptable. There is no anal-lump concept, so Perianal lump is the closest. The two findings are recorded independently, so the pain is not tied to the lump, but that is the best the language allows.
evidence: Urgent: anal symptoms ... :: (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Perianal lump" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Anal pain" "finding") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Severe (severity modifier)" "qualifier value"))))
check_for :: Perianal lump; Anal pain + Severe

elements.problem: 'Unable to pass stool' is encoded as 'Does not defecate' (parent: Finding related to ability to defecate), and 'because of anal symptoms' is expressed by the AND with Anal finding. There is no closer concept for 'unable to defecate'.
Morphine dosing; 'stop if BP < 90/60' is a drug-administration stop rule, not triage.

elements.scope_reason: The page says 'treat for sexually transmitted proctitis', which is a presumptive diagnosis but neither 'likely' nor 'consider'. probable is defensible, possible is also arguable. The 'if anal sex, ask about genital symptoms (p62)' and 'if diarrhoea (p58)' parts are cross_reference_only.
elements.problem: The three alternatives (painless bleeding, passing mucus, tenesmus) are ORed correctly and anchored to anal symptoms. No 'sexually transmitted proctitis' concept exists; 'Infective proctitis' is a reasonable parent and better than the gonococcal-only concept. The 'anal sex' context is not used as evidence, and the page does not make it a condition for treatment.
evidence: Diagnose probable sexually transmitted proctitis from anal symptoms :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Infective proctitis" "disorder") probable) (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Anal finding" "finding")) (or Painless rectal bleeding | Mucus in stool | Tenesmus of anus and/or rectum))

elements.problem: Examination branch 'Crack/s' leads only to management; the page states no 'likely' diagnosis, such as anal fissure.

elements.scope_reason: Contains the flowchart decision 'Suspected worms: is worm flat and white with worm segments (blunt ended)?' ('Lump/pile' is routing only)
parts_missing: The flat/white/segmented-worm decision is not encoded: the Yes branch (tapeworm) is absent and the No branch is not a condition of the pinworm rule
elements.problem: Only the generic 'Worms in stool' finding is captured; the discriminating question the flowchart asks is lost.
Red/raw skin branch leads to management only.
Ulcers/warts branch routes to pages 65 and 68.

'If pile cannot be reduced or is thrombosed, refer' is a referral criterion outside the red box. SNOMED has 'Thrombosed hemorrhoids' if a builder wanted to encode it, but the house standard does not require it.
Wart referral criteria plus cross-references to pages 65 and 68.

elements.scope_reason: 'Tapeworm likely' (Yes branch: worm flat and white with segments)
parts_missing: probable diagnosis of tapeworm infection (e.g. 'Cestode infection' or 'Infection caused by Taenia', both of which exist), with Worms in stool plus the flat/segmented worm as evidence
elements.problem: No rule encodes the tapeworm conclusion. The feature 'flat segmented worm' has no precoordinated finding (only the organisms 'Proglottid of Taenia ...'), so the builders may have dropped it, but it is not noted as not representable in the rules.

elements.scope_reason: 'If worm is thin and white, with anal itch worse at night, pinworm likely' (No branch); the 'other worm or unsure' bullet is treatment only
elements.problem: The rule fires on any worms in stool plus night-time anal itch. A patient with tapeworm segments and night itch would be labelled probable pinworm, against the flowchart. The concept (Enterobiasis), the night-itch qualifier and AND logic are otherwise right.
evidence: Diagnose probable pinworm from anal itch at night :: (diagnosis (snomed_concept "Enterobiasis" "disorder") probable) (and (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Worms in stool" "finding")) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Pruritus ani" "disorder") (qualifier (snomed_concept "Night time" "qualifier value"))))

elements.problem: 'If Hb < 12 (woman) or < 13 (man), anaemia likely (p44)' needs a unitless haemoglobin value; the rest is management and hygiene advice.
Referral criteria for the worm branch (abdominal tenderness, mass, vomiting, larva migrans); no 'likely' or priority wording.

rule_level_problems.problem: The Yes branch of 'Is worm flat and white with worm segments?' → 'Tapeworm likely' is lost entirely; no probable rule and no check_for item for a flat/segmented worm.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable pinworm from anal itch at night
rule_level_problems.problem: It ignores the flowchart branch: pinworm sits on the No branch (worm not flat/segmented, thin and white), but the rule fires on any 'Worms in stool' plus night itch, so a tapeworm patient with night itch would get probable Enterobiasis.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable sexually transmitted proctitis / Urgent priority
rule_level_problems.problem: The page defines tenesmus as 'unable to pass stools despite feeling the need to' (non-urgent proctitis), while the red box's 'unable to pass stool because of anal symptoms' is Urgent. Recording 'Does not defecate' and 'Tenesmus' depends on the health worker telling these apart; nothing in the rules guides it. The proctitis rule is also probable although the page only says 'treat for'.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for urgent anal symptom conditions
rule_level_problems.problem: The anchor 'Anal finding' is not a common symptom or warning sign. The task only fires if anal complaints are recorded under that concept or a descendant (descendants also include 'Anus normal').

summary: The red box is encoded correctly: Urgent = anal finding AND (perianal lump + severe anal pain, OR does not defecate). The proctitis rule matches the page's three ORed triggers. The worm flowchart is the weak point: 'Tapeworm likely' is missing, and the pinworm rule drops the flat/segmented-worm decision, so it would also fire for tapeworm. Anaemia (Hb thresholds) is not representable, and all other outside elements are management or routing.
